findings.text: Primary processor based controls treated as optional cover timestamp exiting, task priority shadowing, IO bitmaps, monitor trapping, MSR bitmaps, NMI windowing, pause exiting, plus activation of the secondary and tertiary layers.

Secondary controls require nothing and optionally span APIC access and delivery virtualization, cache and TLB exit behaviors, process identifiers, extended paging and mode controls, unrestricted execution, pause loop, descriptor, timestamp and random source exits, XSAVES, logging, scaling, wait pause, tracing, function dispatch, bus lock, notification, enclave and virtualization exception behaviors. Tertiary controls require nothing and optionally allow virtualized interprocessor interrupts.

Each VMCS control category keeps a software shadow. Stores write hardware only on change then update shadow. Loads read shadow directly or via the loaded control structure of the vCPU. Bit set, clear and conditional change validate at build time that the bit belongs to required or optional masks for that category, then apply read modify write through the store path.
VMX lazy state covers stack pointer, instruction pointer, flags, page pointer table, segments, control registers zero three and four, and two exit information words.
Enlightened VMCS use is tracked by a static branch flag, with a per CPU accessor exposing the current enlightened control structure derived from the current VMCS pointer.
VMX support headers provide include guards, a helper translating an emulation context to its vCPU container, and an alias routing emulated MSR completion to generic instruction GP completion.

x86 KVM publishes capability and host value globals, core and nested vendor dispatch tables, and widely read tunables for minimum timer period, TSC tolerance, VMware backdoor enable, forced emulation prefix, posted interrupt timer, SMT return mitigation, APIC virtualization, virtual IPI, device posted interrupts, and permission for smaller maximum physical address.
Vendor module selection is serialized by a dedicated mutex guarding installation of vendor specific operations.

Userspace ABI masks define must be zero hypercall bits with one valid hypercall, a PMU disable bit, guest debug enable plus stepping and breakpoint and injection and interrupt blocking bits, cross APIC identifier and broadcast control bits, clock stability and source bits, a broad quirk family with a conditional subset, bus lock detection off and exit modes, and notify exit enable and userspace bits.

Supported guest extended state spans floating point, vector, bound, wide vector, protection key and tile features, while supported supervisor state spans user and kernel control flow enforcement features.

Paravirtual clock state holds mode, last cycle, mask, multiplier, shift, base cycles and offset. Global guest time data holds monotonic and raw copies of that state plus boot offset, wall seconds and a sequence counter, with a single global instance.

VM and vCPU statistics expose descriptor arrays plus headers carrying name size, descriptor count and byte offsets for identifiers, descriptors and data, alongside a dedicated x86 emulator slab cache pointer.

VM counters focus on MMU lifecycle including zapping, write tracking, flooding, recycling, misses, unsync depth, shadow pages, page size residency, splits and hash sizing peaks. vCPU counters focus on page fault handling, TLB maintenance, exit classification, state reloads, emulation outcomes, hypercalls, interrupt injection, nested entry, scheduling hints and guest mode.

Exception contribution classes distinguish benign, contributory and page fault cases with small integer codes. Exception dispositions distinguish fault, trap, abort, interrupt and debug cases with small integer codes.

Extended state and protection key switching skip protected guests, require OS save support for control register handling, synchronize control and supervisor state only on guest host mismatch, and condition key writes on hardware support plus either extended feature or control register enable, saving guest value and restoring host on exit.

Sensitive instruction emulation checks privilege and state, injects general protection or queues undefined vector on failure, otherwise writes split results and advances past the instruction. Monitor and wait either fault as invalid when disabled under quirk dependent feature or misc enable state, or warn once and emulate as no operation.
Exit request check prepares for transfer to guest mode then reports pending when vCPU mode shows exiting, when any request flag is set, or when transfer work is pending.

Global paravirtual time updates run inside a sequence write section copying monotonic and raw clocksource parameters plus wall and boot offsets. Readers sample base cycles plus scaled timestamp delta under optimistic sequence retry and add boot adjusted offset.

TSC rate handling tracks per CPU host rates and a maximum, adjusts rates by tolerance in parts per million, builds nanosecond conversion factors and a tolerance window, selects scaling only outside that window, then programs either a calculated multiplier or catchup mode depending on hardware scaling support and requested direction.

Multiplier writes always record the level one value, combine with the level two factor while a nested guest is active and otherwise use level one directly, then push to hardware when scaling control exists.

Guest timestamp is scaled delta between kernel time and last stamp plus last written value. Time and TSC sampling first checks cached clock mode for timestamp basis then revalidates after a sequence protected base read.

Risky TSC cases include uncalibrated host rate, zero request, below hardware request without scaling support, and out of range calculated ratio, each warned and either rejected or mapped to a safe multiplier or catchup path. Stale time reads must retry on sequence contention.
Optional x86 operation and nested operation declaration forms alias to the base declaration form, including return zero variants, so optionality carries no extra behavior in these fragments.
Whether any guest uses a master clock is tracked by an atomic counter initialized to zero.
Forced emulation prefix reserves one bit requesting clearing of the resume flag, with an integer tunable selecting the prefix behavior.
